exposure: sensitization levels to specific allergens (alpha-lactalbumin, casein, lysozyme)
outcome: composition of intestinal microbiota (e.g., levels of symbionts, Klebsiella spp., Clostridium spp., Enterobacter spp., Escherichia coli lactose-negative, Citrobacter spp., Escherichia coli hemolytic)
cohort: The study included 56 full-term infants aged 6-12 months with food allergy symptoms.
finding: In patients with IgE-mediated allergy, significant positive associations were found between sensitization to specific allergens (alpha-lactalbumin, casein, lysozyme) and the content of hemolytic Escherichia coli and Clostridium spp. in the intestinal microbiota.
